executive_summary: The .husky/pre-commit Stage 1 secret-detection scan builds STAGED_CONTENT (and, separately, FIXTURE_CONTENT for the apa-calibration-fixtures allowlist) from a diff against HEAD only. On a merge commit -- the documented ship path for every fleet worker, who ships from a linked git worktree -- every line the other parent (origin/main) brings in reads as newly ADDED, so main's own pre-existing content is rescanned as if entering the tree, producing false-positive blocks on legitimate merges (witnessed blocking PR #8490 on 2026-09-08). Escalated from QF-20260911-880 (Adam ruling d67d7094: a git-hook edit must run under the full gate set, not as a QF). Three LEAD-phase sub-agent passes (validation-agent 3a0213a7, risk-agent 63e379f0, testing-agent prospective 7f3f5cdf) corrected the mint-time scope on two structural points and found three distinct fail-open failure modes that a naive fix would introduce: (1) the mint-time wording 'when .git/MERGE_HEAD exists' is ALWAYS FALSE inside a git worktree (.git is a file there; MERGE_HEAD lives at .git/worktrees/<name>/MERGE_HEAD) -- the correct test is `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD`; (2) an unsorted `comm -12` intersection silently empties under this hook's `2>/dev/null || true` house style, disabling secret detection fleet-wide rather than merely re-blocking a false positive -- `grep -Fxf` is the sortedness-independent replacement; (3) the fix must cover BOTH content streams (STAGED_CONTENT and FIXTURE_CONTENT), not just one. KNOWN CONSTRAINT carried into EXEC: the auto-mode permission classifier denies every worker-seat WRITE to .husky/pre-commit (measured on the origin QF, same file, 2026-09-11) independent of QF-vs-SD workflow tier -- a seat-class limit per chairman ratification f0b5a482. This PRD's implementation_approach names the escalate-with-ready-patch fallback for that constraint.

functional_requirements.title: Merge-commit-aware basis for STAGED_CONTENT (the primary secret scan)
functional_requirements.description: In .husky/pre-commit's Stage 1 (~line 274), detect an in-progress merge via `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` (exit code only; NEVER a literal `[ -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ]` path test, which is always false inside a git worktree -- .git is a file there, not a directory, and MERGE_HEAD actually lives at .git/worktrees/<name>/MERGE_HEAD). When a merge is detected: build the HEAD-basis added-line set (existing `git diff --cached HEAD --diff-filter=ACM -U0`) and a MERGE_HEAD-basis added-line set (`git diff --cached MERGE_HEAD --diff-filter=ACM -U0`), each filtered to `^+` lines (excluding `^+++` headers) BEFORE any further processing, then intersect the two filtered sets via `grep -Fxf` (fixed-string, line-mode; NOT `comm -12`, which requires sorted input and silently empties on unsorted input under `2>/dev/null || true`). The intersection becomes STAGED_CONTENT for that commit. Non-merge commits keep the existing HEAD-only basis unchanged.

functional_requirements.title: Identical merge-commit-aware basis for FIXTURE_CONTENT (the apa-calibration-fixtures allowlist stream)
functional_requirements.description: FIXTURE_CONTENT (~line 280, the docs/design/apa-calibration-fixtures/* base64-image-line allowlist) is a SEPARATE content stream from STAGED_CONTENT and must receive the identical merge-commit basis treatment (FR-1's rev-parse detection + HEAD/MERGE_HEAD intersection via grep -Fxf), not just the primary stream. Fixing only STAGED_CONTENT leaves a live false-positive (and, if implemented wrong, fail-open) gap in this second stream.

functional_requirements.title: Mandatory non-empty-fallback: never silently scan nothing
functional_requirements.description: If merge detection (`git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD`) errors, or the MERGE_HEAD-basis diff errors, or the FR-1/FR-2 intersection is empty when the HEAD-basis added-line set is non-empty, fall back to the existing HEAD-only basis for that stream rather than proceeding with an empty scanned set. This is NOT a nicety: risk-agent (evidence 63e379f0) and testing-agent (evidence 7f3f5cdf) both independently reproduced that an empty second operand returns empty from grep -Fxf (and from comm -12 alike), and Stage 1 only BLOCKS on a non-empty match set -- so any defect that shrinks the scanned set to empty fails OPEN (silently disables secret detection) rather than fails closed. This is strictly worse than the status-quo bug and must be structurally prevented, not merely tested for.

functional_requirements.title: Regression test suite under tests/unit/husky/ covering all 10 identified cases
functional_requirements.description: New test file(s) under tests/unit/husky/ (NOT tests/unit/hooks/, which does not exist -- husky bash-hook tests live in tests/unit/husky/, per validation-agent evidence 3a0213a7 and testing-agent evidence 7f3f5cdf), following the existing pre-commit-nonempty-index-guard.test.js pattern (vitest + spawnSync('bash', [...]) + bashAvailable() -> describe.skip + fs.mkdtempSync throwaway repo), PLUS a genuine `git worktree add`-based fixture (reusing the pattern at tests/unit/resolve-sd-workdir/worktree-atomicity.test.js and lib/worktree-quota.test.js) for the worktree-shaped cases -- a plain-repo-only test would certify the worktree-inert literal-path bug as passing. Cover all 10 cases in test_scenarios T1-T10 below, including the 3 MUST-FAIL-IF-BROKEN negative controls (T5, T6, T7).

technical_requirements.title: Merge detection: git rev-parse, never a literal MERGE_HEAD path test
technical_requirements.description: Use `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` (exit code 0 = merge in progress). Do NOT use `[ -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ]` or any other literal filesystem path test against `.git/MERGE_HEAD` -- confirmed by validation-agent (evidence 3a0213a7) and independently reproduced by risk-agent and testing-agent that this literal test is always false inside a git worktree, because `.git` there is a FILE (a gitdir pointer), and the real MERGE_HEAD lives at `.git/worktrees/<worktree-name>/MERGE_HEAD`. `git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD` (to get the resolved path) is an acceptable alternative to the exit-code form if the implementation needs the actual path, but the exit-code form (`git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD`) is simpler and sufficient for a boolean 'is a merge in progress' check.

technical_requirements.title: Intersection primitive: grep -Fxf, never comm -12
technical_requirements.description: Use `grep -Fxf <fileA> <fileB>` (fixed-string, whole-line match) to compute the intersection of the two added-line sets. Do NOT use `comm -12`, which REQUIRES both inputs to be sorted; unsorted input makes `comm` print a warning to stderr and emit EMPTY stdout with a non-zero exit code, and this hook's own `2>/dev/null || true` house style silently swallows that failure -- turning a coding mistake into a silent, fleet-wide secret-detection outage rather than a loud test failure. This is the single highest-severity finding from the LEAD-phase risk-agent and testing-agent passes (both independently reproduced it live).

technical_requirements.title: Filter ^+/^+++ BEFORE intersecting, not after
technical_requirements.description: Apply the existing `grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+\+\+'` hunk-marker filter to EACH of the two diffs (HEAD-basis and MERGE_HEAD-basis) independently, BEFORE computing their intersection. Hunk headers (`@@ ... @@`) and file headers differ between the two diffs even for textually-identical content lines, so intersecting the raw (unfiltered) diff output would corrupt the comparison -- filter first, then intersect the filtered `^+` line sets.

technical_requirements.title: No change to SECRET_PATTERNS, no bypass flags
technical_requirements.description: This fix changes only the basis of the added-line scan on merge commits. SECRET_PATTERNS (the regex list) is unchanged; no new bypass flag, env var, or CLI option is introduced; hooks.Stop and permissions.allow are untouched. The guard added in PR #8110 (which makes storeSubAgentResults throw on an empty-evidence blocking verdict, unrelated to this hook but the reason a failed run surfaces loudly elsewhere in the fleet) stays as-is and is not weakened.

technical_requirements.title: EXEC-phase classifier constraint: attempt once, then escalate with the ready patch
technical_requirements.description: The auto-mode permission classifier is known (measured 2026-09-11 on the origin QF-20260911-880, same file, session 64728de4) to deny EVERY worker-seat WRITE to .husky/pre-commit -- both a Bash `sed -i` and the Edit tool -- independent of whether the work ships via a QF or a full SD (a seat-class limit per chairman ratification f0b5a482, not a wording or workflow-tier problem). At EXEC, the implementing worker: (a) writes and lands the new tests/unit/husky/ regression test file normally (ordinary path, not classifier-sensitive), (b) drafts the COMPLETE, ready-to-apply patch text for .husky/pre-commit satisfying FR-1..FR-3/TR-1..TR-4, (c) attempts the actual .husky/pre-commit write ONCE to confirm current classifier behaviour (a capability claim is settled only by attempting it, not by citing a memory of a prior denial), and (d) if denied, signals stuck (severity high) with the complete patch text + test plan in the body and RELEASES the SD claim (not hold -- this is the pre-commit-specific precedent, distinct from the .github/workflows precedent where holding is correct) so a differently-privileged actor can apply the patch directly from this PRD.

test_scenarios.expected: Correctly detects an in-progress merge in BOTH a plain repo and a linked git worktree (via git worktree add); a literal `.git/MERGE_HEAD` path test is proven to fail in the worktree case as a documented negative control.

test_scenarios.scenario: Merge bringing in a pre-existing, already-redacted fixture line (the false positive this SD exists to fix)
test_scenarios.expected: Stage 1 does NOT block -- the merge commit passes.

test_scenarios.scenario: Negative control: a genuinely NEW secret introduced by the same merge commit
test_scenarios.expected: Stage 1 STILL BLOCKS -- proves the fix narrowed the false positive without disabling real detection (the guard from PR #8110 stays live).

test_scenarios.scenario: Non-merge commit, unaffected by this fix
test_scenarios.expected: Existing HEAD-only basis behaviour is unchanged; no regression.

test_scenarios.scenario: MUST-FAIL-IF-BROKEN: an inverted merge-detection guard mutation (e.g. the merge branch and non-merge branch swapped)
test_scenarios.expected: Test FAILS if this mutation is present -- catches a guard that silently empties the scan on non-merge commits or fails to activate on merge commits.

test_scenarios.scenario: MUST-FAIL-IF-BROKEN: an unsorted-intersection-input mutation (e.g. comm -12 reintroduced in place of grep -Fxf)
test_scenarios.expected: Test FAILS if this mutation is present -- catches the measured sortedness fail-open (empty stdout, non-zero exit, silently swallowed by 2>/dev/null || true).

test_scenarios.scenario: MUST-FAIL-IF-BROKEN: MERGE_HEAD detection or diff errors, or the intersection is empty while the HEAD-basis set is non-empty
test_scenarios.expected: The HEAD-only basis is used as a fallback (FR-3) -- test FAILS if the implementation instead proceeds with an empty scanned set (fail-open).

test_scenarios.scenario: FIXTURE_CONTENT (the apa-calibration-fixtures second stream) merge-commit basis
test_scenarios.expected: Gets the identical FR-1/FR-2 treatment as STAGED_CONTENT -- a merge bringing in a pre-existing allowlisted fixture line does not block, and a genuinely new secret in that stream still blocks.

test_scenarios.scenario: Filter-ordering: ^+/^+++ hunk-marker filter applied before intersecting, not after
test_scenarios.expected: Intersecting raw (unfiltered) diffs first would corrupt the comparison via differing hunk headers; the correct order (filter each diff, then intersect) produces the right result.

test_scenarios.scenario: Symmetric pathspec exclusions preserved on both diff bases
test_scenarios.expected: The existing exclusions (hook self-exclusion, .githooks/*, apa-calibration-fixtures base64 allowlist handling) apply identically to both the HEAD-basis and MERGE_HEAD-basis diffs.

acceptance_criteria: A merge bringing in a pre-existing redacted fixture line is NOT blocked by Stage 1 (T2 green).
A newly added line matching SECRET_PATTERNS on the same merge commit IS still blocked (T3 green, negative control).
All 3 MUST-FAIL-IF-BROKEN negative controls (T5 inverted guard, T6 unsorted intersection, T7 empty-fallback) are present and demonstrably fail when the corresponding defect is reintroduced.
Both content streams (STAGED_CONTENT and FIXTURE_CONTENT) receive the identical fix (T8 green).
git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD (never a literal .git/MERGE_HEAD path test) correctly detects merge-in-progress in both a plain repo and a linked worktree (T1 green).
0 existing tests broken; the full tests/unit/husky/ suite is green.
No change to SECRET_PATTERNS; no new bypass flag; hooks.Stop and permissions.allow untouched.

risks.risk: A wrong intersection implementation fails OPEN (silently disables secret detection on a merge) rather than fails closed (re-blocks a false positive) -- strictly worse than the bug this SD fixes, and fleet-wide in blast radius since every worker session's commits run through this same shared hook.
risks.mitigation: FR-3's mandatory non-empty-fallback to the HEAD-only basis, plus TR-2's grep -Fxf (sortedness-independent) instead of comm -12, plus T5/T6/T7 as MUST-FAIL-IF-BROKEN regression tests pinning all three measured fail-open modes.

risks.risk: The permission classifier denies the worker-seat WRITE to .husky/pre-commit at EXEC regardless of QF-vs-SD workflow tier.
risks.mitigation: TR-5: attempt the write once to confirm current behaviour, then if denied, /signal stuck with the complete ready-to-apply patch + test plan and release the SD claim so a differently-privileged actor can apply it directly from this PRD -- never retry the write repeatedly.

risks.risk: A test that only exercises a plain repo (not a linked worktree) would certify the worktree-inert literal-path bug (TR-1's negative case) as passing.
risks.mitigation: FR-4 requires a genuine git worktree add fixture for the worktree-shaped cases (T1), reusing the tests/unit/resolve-sd-workdir/worktree-atomicity.test.js / lib/worktree-quota.test.js pattern.

risks.risk: Fixing only STAGED_CONTENT and leaving FIXTURE_CONTENT on the old HEAD-only basis leaves a live, narrower version of the same false-positive (and potential fail-open) bug.
risks.mitigation: FR-2 and T8 require and verify the identical treatment for both streams.

system_architecture.summary: A single shared, repo-wide git hook (.husky/pre-commit) gains merge-aware diff-basis logic in its existing Stage 1 secret-detection section, plus a new regression test suite. No new files besides the test suite; no schema, RPC, or service changes.
components: .husky/pre-commit Stage 1 (~lines 263-330): STAGED_CONTENT and FIXTURE_CONTENT construction, now merge-aware (FR-1/FR-2/FR-3).
tests/unit/husky/ (new test file(s), FR-4): vitest + spawnSync bash harness, throwaway mkdtemp repo + git worktree add fixture, covering T1-T10.

implementation_approach.summary: Land the regression test suite first (ordinary path), draft the complete .husky/pre-commit patch, attempt the write once, and follow the documented classifier-denial escalation path if it is refused.
steps: Write tests/unit/husky/pre-commit-merge-basis.test.js (or similarly named) implementing T1-T10, including the git-worktree-add fixture for T1's worktree case and the mkdtemp+bash harness for the rest, following the existing pre-commit-nonempty-index-guard.test.js conventions.

Run the new test suite against the CURRENT (unfixed) .husky/pre-commit to confirm it fails exactly where expected (T2 should currently fail; T1's literal-path negative control should confirm the worktree-inert bug) -- proves the tests actually exercise the bug before the fix lands.

Draft the complete .husky/pre-commit patch: TR-1 (git rev-parse merge detection) + TR-2 (grep -Fxf intersection) + TR-3 (filter-then-intersect ordering) + FR-3 (non-empty fallback), applied to BOTH STAGED_CONTENT and FIXTURE_CONTENT (FR-1/FR-2).

Attempt the .husky/pre-commit write via the Edit tool once, to measure current classifier behaviour for this session (TR-5) -- do not assume denial from a prior session's memory without re-attempting.
If the write succeeds: re-run the full tests/unit/husky/ suite (now green), verify no other hook stage regressed, and proceed to a normal PR + auto-merge.

If the write is denied: /signal stuck --severity high with the complete patch text (from step 3) + the test file (already landed in step 1) + this PRD's test plan, then release the SD claim (per TR-5) so a differently-privileged actor can apply the patch directly.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: In a linked worktree, merge origin/main (bringing in a pre-existing redacted AKIA-shaped fixture line); run bash .husky/pre-commit.
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: Stage 1 passes (no false-positive block) -- the bug this SD fixes.

smoke_test_steps.instruction: In the same merge commit, stage a genuinely new line matching a SECRET_PATTERNS entry (e.g. a fresh AKIA-shaped key) and re-run bash .husky/pre-commit.
smoke_test_steps.expected_outcome: Stage 1 still BLOCKS -- proves the fix narrowed the false positive without disabling real detection (green step 1 + green step 2 would mean the scanner is off, not fixed).
